results.name: family_leeds_budget
results.reply: I've weighted the search for a family with young children and a £350k budget, and filtered to areas with typical prices at or under that. Garforth East, Meanwood and Primley Park & Wigton Moor score highest, with strong health, environment and schools. Primley Park's typical price sits right at your limit, so expect little room to spare. Hyde Park & Woodhouse Cliff is the cheapest and scores well on amenities, but its score is less stable, so check it closely before deciding.

results.name: commuter_manchester
results.reply: The commuter weighting puts transport first, so the top results are inner-city neighbourhoods close to the centre, such as New Islington and University North. Several of them score low on safety, so check that against your priorities. Sale Central and the Timperley areas are further out but score higher on safety, schools and community, which may be the better trade-off if you can accept a longer journey.

results.name: retiree_devon
results.reply: I ranked the North Devon council area, since the tool resolved "Devon" to that council rather than the whole county. Fremington & Instow (67.8) stands out for safety at 83, and Roundswell & Landkey has the strongest safety score in the list, though it is weaker on amenities. Barnstaple's central areas are busier, with lower safety scores. If you'd like the rest of Devon, such as South Hams or Teignbridge, tell me which part and I'll rank that instead.

results.name: safest_bristol
results.reply: The safest-scoring neighbourhoods within 10 km of Bristol are mostly on its edges, in South Gloucestershire and North Somerset, not in the city itself. Westbury-on-Trym is the only Bristol City neighbourhood in the top eight (rank 3). Downend North scores highest on safety, and the list is on the map. Safety scores are benchmarked within England, so they compare well across the whole region. If you want only the city's own neighbourhoods, I can rank again with a tighter radius around the centre.

results.name: brighton_street_level_budget
results.reply: I've listed the top 10 small areas within 10 km of Brighton with typical prices under £400k (87 qualified), all in Brighton and Hove. Seven Dials, Goldsmid East and Withdean Woods lead on the balanced weighting. Several have strong transport and amenities scores but weaker housing scores, so check the price-to-space trade-off on the profiles. Ask me to narrow this to a particular family or lifestyle preset if you have one.

results.name: young_professional_london
results.reply: I've weighted this toward transport, nightlife and cafés, plus fast broadband. The top results are Rotherhithe, East Village, Leamouth, Millwall South and Clapham Common West, all strong on transport and amenities. Trade-offs: safety scores are mid-range across the list, and Clapham and Earlsfield are the priciest. East Village or Rotherhithe look like the best value for a night-out lifestyle. Tell me your budget or which parts of London you'd commute to and I can narrow it.

results.name: profile_postcode
results.reply: LS6 3AA is in Headingley, Leeds. It scores 65.7, better than 72% of neighbourhoods across the UK and Ireland. It excels on amenities, GP access and transport, but safety is among the weakest in the index, with burglary and theft well above typical levels. Sunshine is also low. If safety matters most to you, compare it with nearby Leeds neighbourhoods.

results.name: profile_place
results.reply: Whitley Bay (the Promenade area, a small neighbourhood of about 1,700 people) scores 59.1, better than 43% of all scored neighbourhoods in the UK and Ireland. It stands out for amenities, schools and health services, and has good sports and cultural facilities. Safety is the weak spot: crime rates sit in the bottom few percent of England, and housing and community scores are also low. Whitley Bay is a wider town, so you may want to compare other parts of it before deciding.

results.name: compare_two
results.reply: Chapel Allerton here means the Chapel Allerton North neighbourhood, so that's the one compared. Chapel Allerton North scores slightly higher overall (70.5 vs 68.3). Headingley leads on amenities and nightlife and on transport, while Chapel Allerton North is stronger on safety (notably burglary), schools and environment. Headingley is more expensive to live in on balance, with a lower housing score. Headingley is also much denser, which suits a lively, urban feel.

results.name: compare_three_bristol
results.reply: Clifton Village (74.0) scores highest overall, with strong schools and community scores, while Redland & St Andrew's (71.0) is close behind, with better health services but a lower education score. Bedminster (61.5) trails mainly on safety, where its violent-offence rate is far higher, and on community, though it is the cheapest of the three. Clifton and Redland are both expensive, and housing affordability is weak in both.

results.name: well_run_pubs
results.reply: Within about 500 m of SW1A 1AA there are eight well-run pubs, all rated 5 by the Food Standards Agency. The Phoenix is closest at about 260 m, and Duke of York is the furthest at about 480 m. A rating covers food hygiene only, not the beer or atmosphere.

results.name: nearest_gp
results.reply: The nearest GP is City Health Centre (M1 1PL), about 780 m from M1 1AE, though Ancoats Urban Village Medical Practice and New Islington Medical Centre (both M4 6EE) are about 770 m away, just slightly closer in straight-line terms. The Doc's Surgery (M1 3LY) is about 860 m away. Distances are straight-line, so check the practice's catchment and whether it is accepting new patients before you register.

results.name: explain_safety_gmp
results.reply: The Castlefield & Deansgate small area scores 7.5 on safety, driven mainly by violent and sexual offences (about 84 per 1,000 residents a year) and serious road collisions nearby, which score near zero. The index divides crime by residents, so a city-centre area with few residents and many visitors and workers looks worse than it may feel. Crime figures here are also imputed for Greater Manchester, so treat them as approximate.

results.name: explain_high_score
results.reply: Hampstead's score is driven by access: transport (95), amenities (100) and schools (88) are all near the top, plus close GP, pharmacy and station distances. It is held back by safety (18) and housing affordability (15), where crime rates and a typical house price of about £1.39m score very low. The profile resolves to the Hampstead Town neighbourhood, which scores 72, while the small area shown scores 67 (better than 77% of all areas). Under the balanced weighting, the strengths outweigh the weak safety and price scores.

results.name: least_noise_london
results.reply: The quietest London neighbourhoods by road and rail noise are Belsize Park (Camden), Furzedown West (Wandsworth), Homerton North (Hackney), West Norwood West & Streatham East (Lambeth) and Tufnell Park East (Islington). Belsize Park has the lowest share of homes exposed, about 6%. The search covered areas within 10 km of central London, so a few results may sit just outside the borough boundaries. Noise is one factor among several, and Belsize Park scores low on housing affordability, so check the other themes before you decide.

results.name: map_layer_air
results.reply: The map is now coloured by nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), the air-quality measure the index scores; the list shows the cleanest areas first, mostly rural places in Ireland. PM2.5 is the other scored air-quality measure, and I can colour by that instead if you prefer. Many of these top results are very small, so check population before relying on them.

results.name: shortlist_add
results.reply: I've saved Headingley (the Leeds neighbourhood) to your shortlist.

results.name: what_is_measured_schools
results.reply:
The index's schools and childcare theme is called "education", and it measures:

- **Good primary schools nearby** (England only, scored)
- **Good secondary schools nearby** (England, Wales and Scotland, scored)
- **Choice of good schools** (all nations, scored)
- **Good nurseries nearby** (all nations, scored)

Primary and secondary exam results are shown as context only and don't count toward the score. Ask if you'd like the full detail on how each is calculated.

results.name: compare_top_two_followup
results.reply: Garforth East and Far Headingley & Weetwood are almost tied overall (71.65 vs 71.51), but they trade off differently. Garforth East is stronger on safety and housing affordability, with a lower typical price and lower violent-crime figures, while Far Headingley & Weetwood leads on health services, amenities and transport, with a supermarket and GP closer by. Far Headingley is the more urban option; Garforth East is quieter and cheaper, so your priorities should decide between them.

results.name: profile_then_compare_agree
results.reply: Chapel Allerton North scores slightly higher overall (70.5 against Headingley's 69.5), though it is a larger neighbourhood, so the levels aren't identical. Headingley leads clearly on amenities and transport, while Chapel Allerton North is stronger on schools, environment and burglary, and has more families and lower density. Headingley is cheaper to buy into (£265k against £317k typical), but its burglary rate is about twice as high.

results.name: profile_percentile_is_the_small_areas
results.reply: Headingley's small area (Leeds 044A) scores 69.5, better than 84% of all scored neighbourhoods in the index. It is strongest on amenities, with cafés, restaurants, pubs and a supermarket all close, and on health services and transport. Safety is the weak point, with burglary and road collisions both scoring poorly, and sunshine is low. Its neighbourhood score is 68.3, which is the figure a ranking would show.

results.name: cheapest_of_those
results.reply: Longwell Green & Oldland Common is the most affordable of the top eight, with a median house price of about £329,000. Downend South (about £379,000) and Emersons Green (about £385,000) are the next cheapest.

results.name: reweight_followup
results.reply: Weighted for retirees (safety, health access, environment, and sunshine and quiet count for more; schools count for less), Wigginton now ranks first, with South Bank & Dringhouses and Haxby close behind. Haxby's health score is especially strong, and Strensall stands out for safety, though both have weaker transport and amenities. Bishopthorpe & Copmanthorpe scores very high on safety, but its median price is the highest of the top eight. The map shows these results.

results.name: ambiguous_clapham
results.reply: I used Clapham in Lambeth, London, since it's the best-known; the search also found Clapham Junction, Bedford, North Yorkshire, West Sussex and Devon. This small area scores 60.2, better than 48% of the UK and Ireland. It's strongest on amenities, transport, climate and schools, and weakest on safety (theft, vehicle crime and road collisions) and housing affordability. If you meant a different Clapham, tell me which one.

results.name: ambiguous_newport

If you meant another Newport (Isle of Wight, Shropshire or Pembrokeshire), tell me and I'll look at that one.

results.name: edinburgh_ranking
results.reply: Using the balanced weighting, the top-scoring neighbourhoods in and around Edinburgh are Marchmont West, Canonmills and New Town North, Marchmont East and Sciennes, Bruntsfield, and Stockbridge, all in the city's central south and north-west areas. results.name: glasgow_profile
results.reply: Hyndland falls in the Dowanhill neighbourhood, and the small area profiled is Dowanhill - 01, which scores 74.3 and is better than 94% of all scored areas in the UK and Ireland. It is strong on schools, health services, amenities and environment, but weak on housing affordability (typical price about £411k), climate sunshine, and nearby road collisions. Its safety score is middling.

results.name: belfast_ranking
results.reply: The top-scoring neighbourhoods on the balanced weighting are in the east and south-east of the city: Ormiston P, Lisnasharragh R and Lisnasharragh P, all scoring well on transport, community and health. results.name: bt_postcode_profile

results.name: dublin_ranking
results.reply: The top results are all in south Dublin, mostly Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown around Stillorgan, Blackrock and Terenure, and they score well on health, transport and amenities. Their safety scores are more modest, and the ranking can't include housing or education for these areas, so check those separately before deciding. Ranking is by the balanced weighting, so tell me your priorities, such as schools or price, and I can re-rank.

results.name: ranelagh_profile
results.reply: I used Ranelagh, the Dublin suburb, and its small area scores better than 94% of Ireland. It's strong on transport, health services, amenities, community and climate, but weak on safety (burglary and theft) and environment (noise, and few protected green spaces or good bathing waters nearby). Schools and housing aren't scored in Ireland, so those aren't in the headline. If you tell me what matters most to you, I can reweight the index and compare Ranelagh with nearby areas.

results.name: ireland_retirees
results.reply: I used the retiree weighting across all of Ireland's neighbourhoods. The top results cluster in south Dublin (Stillorgan, Blackrock, Rathfarnham, Terenure) and Cork City (Tramore B, Ballinlough, Browningstown), with strong health and transport scores. Housing and school scores are missing for these areas, so affordability and schools aren't reflected in the ranking. Check house prices and the specific towns you're considering before deciding.

I can rank Dublin neighbourhoods by their overall score or by another theme, such as safety or amenities, if that would help.

results.name: ranelagh_dublin_profile

Schools and housing aren't scored for Ireland yet, so they're left out of the overall.

results.name: republic_of_ireland_ranking

results.name: off_topic
results.reply:
Here's a short poem for you:

Soft paws across the windowsill,
Eyes like lamps that glow and fill
The quiet room with slow delight,
A purring engine, warm and bright.

They dream in sunbeams, stretch and yawn,
Then pounce on shadows, swift as dawn.
Aloof, they choose when to be near,
And curl up close when night is here.

I haven't checked other parts of Harrogate, so if you want a price for a particular street or district, give me the postcode and I'll look it up.

results.name: analyst_sql
